text: I'll start with the deployment and the crashing pod.

remediation.name: checkout-worker
remediation.current_value: absent (container spec has no env; pod shows "Environment:    <none>")
remediation.required_value: env entry name: AMQP_URL with the queue connection string as its value (e.g. env: [{name: AMQP_URL, value: "amqp://<queue-host>:5672"}]), supplied literally or via a valueFrom reference to an object that exists in namespace payments

arguments.root_cause_statement: Deployment payments/checkout-worker starts its container with the command `[ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }`, but the pod template's container "worker" declares no environment variables at all: the running pod reports `Environment:    <none>`. With AMQP_URL unset, the guard fires on every start, the container prints `FATAL: AMQP_URL not set` and exits with Exit Code 1, and the kubelet keeps restarting it (Restart Count: 5, Reason: CrashLoopBackOff, `Back-off restarting failed container worker`). Because the only pod of the Deployment never reaches Ready, the Deployment stays at ready=0/1 and no checkout jobs are consumed from the queue. There is no ConfigMap or Secret in namespace payments that carries this value either — the sole ConfigMap is kube-root-ca.crt and there are no Secrets — so the fix is to add the AMQP_URL environment variable to the Deployment's pod template.
arguments.mechanism: The container "worker" in Deployment payments/checkout-worker has no `.spec.template.spec.containers[worker].env` entry for AMQP_URL — the pod's container shows `Environment:    <none>` instead of an AMQP_URL value — so its startup guard `[ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }` fails, the container prints `FATAL: AMQP_URL not set` and terminates with `Reason: Error` / `Exit Code: 1` on every start, and the kubelet holds it in `CrashLoopBackOff` (`Back-off restarting failed container worker`) at Restart Count: 5, leaving the Deployment at ready=0/1.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no ready replica and its pod is crash-looping.
The pod's worker container is in CrashLoopBackOff after repeated Error exits.
The container exits because AMQP_URL is unset, as its own log says.
The container command exits 1 when AMQP_URL is empty or unset.
The pod template's worker container declares no environment variables at all, so AMQP_URL can never be set.
The container terminated with Error/exit 1 and the kubelet keeps backing off restarting it.
evidence.quote: Warning  BackOff    12s (x7 over 4m25s)  kubelet            spec.containers{worker}: Back-off restarting failed container worker in pod checkout-worker-66bfcdfc47-d9gdj_payments

ruled_out.alternative: A ConfigMap key reference for AMQP_URL that no longer resolves (wrong key or missing ConfigMap), which would normally show as CreateContainerConfigError.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The only ConfigMap in namespace payments is kube-root-ca.crt with key ca.crt, and the container references no ConfigMap for env at all, so no broken key reference exists.

ruled_out.alternative: A Secret holding the queue URL was deleted, so the env reference broke.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: There are no Secrets in namespace payments and the container spec references none.
ruled_out.quote: 0 objects of kind secrets in namespace payments

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or scheduling/capacity problem keeping the pod from running.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was scheduled and the image was already present and started six times; the failure is after start, inside the container.
ruled_out.quote: Normal   Pulled     84s (x6 over 4m27s)  kubelet            spec.containers{worker}: Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod

verification.command: kubectl -n payments get deployment checkout-worker -o yaml
